account: It is one o'clock on day 0, and I have returned to town hall for my town-accounts appointment. This morning I attended the market walk and asked several residents for news; all three said they had none. I have had a feeling that something is happening without me, but have not yet found concrete evidence of a hidden activity. The secretary's mention of two appointment books initially seemed unusual. She explained that she made a provisional office record while I held the original, and that it is not a different schedule. She went to the dockside cottage to confirm my tea appointment, whose original entry lacked an address. The neighbour confirmed tea at three at the cottage at (16, -60, 105). Those matters now appear to be ordinary appointment administration rather than evidence of a secret plan. The secretary is waiting near the office, and the builder is nearby carrying a lantern; I do not know why the builder is here. Several townsfolk are outside town hall. I heard indistinct conversation on returning, but cannot infer its subject. My next business is the accounts, followed by tea and my half-past-four office appointment. I should remain attentive to what residents actually report rather than assume these ordinary movements conceal something.
